reason: coremltools is a pip-installable converter whose documented PyTorch conversion workflow runs on CPU-only Linux with a tiny model.
demo: README Install + Guide 'Converting from PyTorch' (ct.convert on a traced torch model, save .mlpackage)
goal: Install coremltools (from the clone or pip) with PyTorch and scikit-learn, using a Python/torch combination that coremltools supports and that works on Linux x86 CPU. Then make this work: trace a small torch.nn model with torch.jit.trace, convert it with ct.convert(..., convert_to='mlprogram') using a TensorType input named 'x', save it as an .mlpackage, and also convert a scikit-learn LinearRegression via ct.converters.sklearn.convert and save it. Prediction needs macOS and is not required; conversion and saving must work without errors on Linux.
check: A hidden script converts a small conv/linear torch model to an mlprogram package and a sklearn model, then checks the saved files and model spec contents.
